findings.summary: Sign-in continuation now accepts the invitation automatically, so invitees who sign in from an invitation become connected without ever going through the explicit ConsentPanel accept step.
findings.evidence:
- Login continuation preserves a validated invitation without consuming it
+ Login continuation from an invitation accepts it for the invitee once sign-in succeeds, so they land on the new connection

findings.summary: The new ConsentPanel description limits it to invitees who are already signed in, which contradicts its unchanged cardinality of 'exactly one after validation' (every validated invitation).
findings.evidence:
cardinality: exactly one after validation
+ description: Shown to invitees who open the invitation while already signed in

findings.summary: Accepting the invitation during sign-in redeems it before the post-login checks for self-connection, block and replay that the consent criterion depends on, and its failure list only covers provider unavailability.
findings.evidence: claim: "Invite fixture covers acceptance, including acceptance at sign-in, expiry, replay, self-connection, block and simultaneous redemption"; failure: [Provider unavailable shows the shared ErrorSummary]
